analysis.title: Weekly commentary: Midterms and AI in focus at 2027 Forum (November 9, 2026)
key_insights: U.S. stocks rallied the day after the midterm elections, sold off sharply on Thursday and steadied on Friday. The Nasdaq entered correction territory (a decline of at least 5% from its previous peak) as concerns over the AI buildout intensified.

BII's 2027 Outlook Forum conclusion: the AI story is moving into a more nuanced phase. The focus is shifting from pricing the conviction that the buildout must happen to assessing its size and speed relative to how fast AI is adopted across tasks.

A material slowdown in AI spending in 2027, though far from certain, could have significant adverse market consequences. It could also ease competition for capital, lower bond yields and temper policy initiatives through its economic fallout.
This two-sided uncertainty underpinned BII's move to neutral on U.S. equities and its upgrade of U.S. Treasuries last month.
Democrats took control of both the House and Senate in the midterms.
The supply-driven regime BII has described for five years is largely priced in, which makes the outlook less directional and more nuanced.

Forum debates on AI covered how much capacity will be built, whether adoption demand justifies the investment, when opportunities shift from suppliers to adopters, and who captures the gains versus who gets disrupted. Corporate CFOs presented how they deploy AI and assess its benefits.

Competition for capital is a major theme: AI financing needs collide with government borrowing and investment in energy security and defense. Portfolio managers debated crowding out of other borrowers and whether greater equity issuance could help hyperscalers manage leverage and preserve borrowing capacity.

Last week's Nasdaq 100 fell 4.7%, leaving it 14% below its October peak. The S&P 500 fell 2.4%. 10-year Treasury yields fell 13 basis points to 4.86%. Brent crude fell 17% to $97 a barrel on hopes for an end to the Middle East conflict.
Week ahead: U.S. CPI (Nov. 10) and PPI (Nov. 13) come before the Fed's December meeting. BII expects persistent inflation pressures to keep market expectations for further Fed rate hikes alive.
Last week's U.S. payrolls report was strong.

Tactical positioning (6-12 months): neutral U.S., Europe, UK, Japan and China equities, overweight emerging market equities, overweight short-term U.S. Treasuries, neutral long-term Treasuries, underweight long-term IG credit and Japanese government bonds, overweight EM local currency debt.

sector_views.rationale: AI fundamentals are strong, but BII expects near-term volatility. It favors AI- and tech-related opportunities while staying neutral on U.S. equities overall.
BII favors these sectors within a neutral Europe view.
Scarcity, secure supply and power demand carry inflation risks, which BII expresses through infrastructure, energy bottlenecks and real-asset-linked exposures.

risk_factors: A material slowdown in AI capital spending in 2027 before productivity gains from adoption materialize.
Competition for capital from AI financing, government borrowing, energy security and defense could crowd out other borrowers and push yields higher.
Policy uncertainty could fuel near-term U.S. equity volatility.
Persistent inflation could keep expectations for further Fed rate hikes alive.
Credit markets are becoming more selective, with tight spreads and uneven fundamentals.
Heavy issuance and further rate hikes could push Japanese government bond yields higher.

tension_points.bear_case: A material slowdown in AI spending in 2027 could have significant adverse market consequences, and the size and speed of the buildout may outrun adoption.
